newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA TOTAL FARM OUTPUT 1.8 PCT UP IN 1996.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA TOTAL FARM OUTPUT 1.8 PCT UP IN 1996.

text.p: Romania's total farm output last year rose by 1.8 percent on 1995, estimates released by the National Statistics Board (CNS) on Friday showed.

A CNS report said arable output -- including grains, sunflower, sugar beet, potatoes and fruit -- increased by 1.9 percent in 1996, with output in the animal breeding sector rising 1.7 percent on 1995.
Romania's farm output was 4.1 percent up in 1995 on the previous year.
The CNS said Romania's grain harvest last year was lower than in 1995, while most other crops saw increases.

The 1996 grain crop dropped by about 5.7 million tonnes to 14.2 million, mainly due to a failure to complete autumn sowing work on wheat and barley and to adverse weather, which badly hit wheat, rye and barley crops, the report said.
It also said the arable area last year stood at 8.8 million hectares, some 400,000 ha less than in 1995.

Wheat and rye output sagged to around 3.2 million tonnes in 1996, less than half the previous year's level, while the barley and two-row barley harvest was 709,000 tonnes down at 1.1 million, preliminary data showed.
Last year's maize crop was slightly down on 1995 at 9.6 million tonnes.
The sunflower crop was up by 163,000 tonnes to 1.09 million tonnes, soybeans output rose by around 5,000 tonnes to 113,000 tonnes and sugar beet output was 194,000 tonnes up at 2.8 million tonnes.
The report said the private sector accounted for 83.2 percent of the 1996 grain crop, 68.9 percent of sunflower output and 80.6 percent of the sugar beet harvest.
It also said that according to preliminary data the number of cattle at end-1996 had risen by some 200,000 on 1995 to 3.7 million and the number of pigs was 167,000 up at 8.1 million.
The number of sheep and goats in 1996 dropped by 600,000 from the previous year to 10.5 million, CNS data showed.
The CNS said at end-1996 private farmers had 90.9 percent of the cattle and 58.4 percent of the pigs. It also held 93.1 percent of sheep and goats.
